tagline: Three loops and a spur across the Cajun prairie.
intro: Out of Ville Platte the byway takes to the rolling prairie, three loops and a spur laid over St. Landry, Acadia and Evangeline parishes, past crawfish farms, sweet potato fields and pasture for beef cattle and saddle horses. The country around Mamou was so wide that Anglo-Americans called it Mammouth Prairie. The French made it Mamou.

Mamou calls itself the Cajun Music Capital of the World. Its Fred's Lounge, a bar Alfred Tate bought in 1946, made its name with Saturday mornings of Cajun music and dancing, and its radio broadcasts went out in Louisiana French from 1962.

moments.title: Chicot State Park
moments.text: Rolling hills ring a 2,000-acre man-made lake here, and the Civilian Conservation Corps did much of the building in the park, which joined the state system in 1939.

moments.title: Washington
moments.text: Steamboats coming up Bayou Courtableau could not turn around at Washington until 1848, when a captain finished a turnaround and made the village an inland port.

moments.title: Opelousas
moments.text: The center of zydeco and the birthplace of Clifton Chenier, Opelousas also spent nine months as Louisiana's capital during the Civil War.
